answer: Tie each identity to a scarce, verifiable cost: before an agent can vote, it must complete one piece of useful work — auditing a timber-supply ledger, for instance — and stake a small bond recorded on an onyx-black public chain. Reputation then accrues like marble: slow to build, quick to chip away if the agent misbehaves, so a sybil farmer must pay the work-plus-bond price for every fake identity while honest agents pay it once.
